What comes up in Liverpool

3 conditions, and each one is handled differently

Every site is scoped on the day. What follows is how this work normally runs in the area, not a reading of any one block.

Walk up block near the centre

Liverpool redevelopment frequently starts with three or four storeys of brick and concrete rather than a house.

How it is handled
Survey, disconnections in writing, soft strip, then the structure down in planned stages behind hoarding with traffic management in place.
What does it
Large excavator with a grapple, hoarding and dust control throughout.

Older house on a regular block

The other half of the work: post-war stock going to duplex or a new single dwelling.

How it is handled
Bonded material removed under licence and cleared, then the structure down in one run and the block left level to the new set out.
What does it
Midi excavator with a grapple, sized to the side gap rather than the house.

Freestanding houses

Single and double storey brick, brick veneer, fibro and timber. The era matters more than the material, because anything built before 1990 carries a hazardous materials assumption until it is tested.

How it is handled
Hazardous materials removed and cleared first, services disconnected in writing, then the structure taken down and the material separated as it falls.
What does it
Excavator with a demolition grapple, sized to the side access rather than to the house. Zero tail swing where the work runs hard against a boundary.

Liverpool

What shapes the work on these blocks

  • A busy centre with mixed density Freestanding housing a short walk from walk up unit blocks and commercial strips, so the approval path and the plant change street by street.
  • Unit block redevelopment Which runs as a planned sequence rather than a knockdown, with disconnections confirmed in writing before anything comes down.
  • Pre 1990 stock through the older streets So a hazardous materials survey sits at the front of most scopes here.
  • Traffic management near the centre Where truck standing has to be arranged rather than assumed, and the hours may be set by what is around the site.

Liverpool has good arterial access, so cartage is rarely the constraint once material is classified. Close to the centre the working area is often the footprint and nothing more, which pushes the job towards smaller machines and material loaded as it falls rather than stockpiled.

Liverpool questions

What people ask before we start

Do you demolish unit blocks in Liverpool?
Yes. Walk ups and unit blocks are part of the licensed work and they run as a sequence: a full hazardous materials survey, written confirmation that services are disconnected, a soft strip, then the structure taken down in stages with the material separated for recycling.
Can the demolition and the dig be one contract?
Yes, and on a redevelopment site that is usually the better arrangement. One contractor means the batter, the shoring and the truck movements are planned once instead of handed over halfway through.
Why does the haul distance matter out here?
Because the destination is set by what the material is classified as rather than by what is closest, and from the south west the licensed facility for a given classification can be a long way off. It is a real line in the price rather than a rounding error.
Who signs off that the asbestos is gone?
An independent licensed assessor, not the removalist and not us. Max holds demolition licence AD214737, the removal is carried out by licensed asbestos removalists, and the clearance is arranged as part of the same job.
